courses.title: Interprofessional Learning for Social Work in Health Care
courses.description: This course enables students to explore, in an interprofessional context, the social issues in the health care and understand the roles and functions of social work in health care system. A primary objective is to provide students with innovative, cross-disciplinary, team-based learning experience which involves medicine, nursing, pharmacy, public health and other health profession to develop knowledge, skills and attitudes related to competence in interprofessional collaboration, foster interprofessional teamwork in health care, and prepare them for careers across healthcare-relevant practice settings.

2. health care policy and social issues related to health care
3. common health care problems during aging
4. health care promotion, disease treatment and prevention
5. health care education to service users in laymen language
6. roles and functions of different healthcare service providers

courses.title: Service-learning Online Course
courses.description: This online course aims to provide students with an overview of Service-Learning (S-L), including its definition, its relevant concepts and theories, and its implications for the good of society and enhancement of personal development. Through different online materials and interactive exercises, students can learn how to assess the needs of different communities, define objectives, design service projects creatively, implement the projects to meet these needs, and develop methods to evaluate the outcomes. Students will be encouraged to reflect on how the knowledge and skills that they have acquired in their own disciplines may facilitate the development of S-L projects. It is designed in the form of self-paced e-Learning modules which can be taken as a standalone prerequisite to students’ self-initiated service projects.

courses.title: Social Work and Cultural Diversity
courses.description:
(UGEC2684 is double-coded with SOWK2202.)

This course provides students with fundamental and systematic knowledge on issues related to ethnic and cultural diversity. Apart from introducing contemporary theories and conceptual perspectives about cultural sensitivity and cultural intelligence, this course will also highlight major discourses and challenges concerning access, equity, social inclusiveness, cultural assimilation and integration which have substantial impact on ethnic minorities as well as social harmony. Through participation in small group projects, guided community tours, and face-to-face interaction with different ethnic groups, students will be able to develop an awareness of the differences in values, beliefs, life-style and interpersonal relatedness between themselves and people of other ethnic background. Basic skills, knowledge and attitude required of cultural intelligence, equal-opportunity legislations, social policies, service provision in meeting the needs of ethnic minorities, and measures to promote mutual acceptance and social inclusiveness will be discussed.

1. Background and global trend of cultural diversity

a. Globalization and Ethnic Diversity

b. Culture, Ethnicity and Diversity

c. Impacts of culture on economy, health, education, immigration, social service, community development, public policy and social harmony

2. Major perspectives in cultural diversity and Intercultural Intelligence

a. “Person-in-environment” Perspective

b. Multi-culturalism

c. The Intercultural Perspective

3. Understanding ethnic and culture groups in Hong Kong

a. Major Ethnic and Cultural Groups in Hong Kong

b. Cultural Barriers and Dilemmas faced by members of ethnic minority groups

c. Stress, vulnerability, strengths and resilience in ethnic and migrant groups

d. Access and Equity

4. Cross-culture assessment and cultural formation

5. Development of cultural sensitivity, cultural competence and intercultural intelligence

courses.title: Global Justice, International Order and Policy Building
courses.description:
Globalization not only brings significant impact on economic development but also significantly redefines norms and values. From the Universal Declaration of Human Rights being ratified in 1949 to the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development Goals adopted in 2015, international mechanisms, such as the United Nations, have constantly constructed social values under prerequisite global power order among nations. Globalization shapes international value and policy setting, political power among nation states and intergovernmental organizations influences local policy environment that goes beyond the regulation of nation state.
This course offers an opportunity for the students to understand three levels of human rights development: ideology, political interplay, and policy formulation. Through exploring the causes and constructions of human rights, this course sets the grounds for students to comprehend knowledge on the current human rights and policy debates concerning social citizenship in relations to the underlying process of the international mechanisms and power relationships. Judging from the debates, students will also explore and analyze globalization and the regional impact on a variety of actors in social policy and on local policymaking.
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Globalization and human rights development

2. Dimensions of human rights and their interplay

3. The development and making of social policy

4. International values and their application on local policymaking

5. The roles and functions of international human rights mechanisms and international organizations

6. Regional mechanisms in human right governance and regional policy setting

7. Poverty, human rights and humanitarianism

8. Women’s rights, gender equality and movements

9. What is global equality and justice: who defines whose rights?

10. Culture, religion and human rights: co-existence or contradictory?

11. Putting discussions into action: how human rights organizations influence policy

12. Globalization, glocalization, localization: the future impact of globalization on local policy

courses.title: Research in Social Welfare and Social Work
courses.description: This course is designed to provide the students with an understanding and appreciation of scientific and evidence-based approach to build knowledge for professional social work practice and evaluate practice in a variety of social services settings. Research processes examine in stages from problem formulation to analyses. The course focuses on how research problems are formulated, hypotheses or research questions are derived, the specific designs that practice researchers may use in addressing given research topics, and data collection and analysis approaches, and evaluating the research of others. The theoretical concepts, approaches, methods and issues in qualitative and quantitative research are covered.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Social Work
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students will be able to:
1. Develop an understanding on the conceptual foundations and methodological tools of quantitative and qualitative social research and its application to the fields of social welfare and social work.
2. Identify and discuss ethical issues related to research design and the reporting and use of research results.
3. Select appropriate quantitative and/or qualitative research methods to study a vulnerable population or a social problem, and be aware of their strengths and weaknesses.
4. Become familiar with basic qualitative and quantitative data analysis techniques in social work research.
5. Critically discuss and evaluate service programs, welfare policies, and research of others.
6. Conduct social work research at the postgraduate level in an independent manner.

courses.subject: SOWK
courses.title: Digital Transformation in Social Services
courses.description:
To address the digital transformation challenges faced by social services agencies, alignment of ICT strategy with organisation reality across all levels involves the development of a roadmap for ICT adoption and organisation transformation. Practitioners need knowledge and skills to grow their digital competency over time in adapting to the latest digital landscape for delivering more engaging social services.
The purpose of this course is to help students navigate the digital transformation maze through sound program/project management in an evidence-based context. The main goals of digital transformation are needs and competencies assessment, workflow change, and system integration of logic models in supporting data driven decision making. Social service agencies have to put the data in order and equip operation staff with the needed knowledge and skills to function effectively and efficiently.
Use of design thinking and lean startup approach will be integrated into digital social services development and implementation as covered in this course. Furthermore, students will learn to use no-code/low-code digital tools to implement a fully integrated data driven information management and service system. The completed system can be used for ongoing data collection, statistical analysis, and data visualisation for event promotion, service program tracking, volunteer recruitment, impact evaluation, donation accounting, and funding application.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Programmes allowed to enrol: MA Fam Counselling & Fam Edu, MA Social Policy, MA Social Service Management, MSSc Social Work, Master of Social Work and MPhil-PhD Social Welfare.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking the course, students will be able to:

1) Understand the current digital landscape and disruptions facing social services agencies.

2) Assess digital application needs using an integrated design thinking and lean startup approach for managing transformation projects and making sustainable and scalable impacts.

3) Write up application requirement specifications for fostering innovative design and prototype development of a data driven information management and service system.

4) Utilise no-code/low-code digital workflow tools to implement an integrated database system for further stakeholder validation and program evaluation.

5) Collect data and device relevant statistical measures for further data analysis and visualisation with impact assessment and funding application consideration.
courses.course_syllabus:
* *Module 1 - Understanding the Digital Transformation Landscape**

* Overview of the disruptive changes to our lives and works caused by the rapidly changing digital landscape with constant innovation found in artificial intelligence/robotics, blockchain, cloud computing/IoT, big data, and immersive technologies.
* Describe how performing data aggregation and data management with digital technologies has become a critical organisational competency for developing an evidence based practice.
* Describe the digital transformation challenges for building the new competency and the implications for social service agencies.

* *Module 2 - Social Innovation with the Lean Startup Methods**

* Overview of the Theory of Change and social innovation at the BOP (Bottom of the Pyramid).
* Introduce the Lean Startup method and how it has been used to build innovative social products and services with a sustainable and scalable social business model.
* Describe the use of low-code/no-code digital tools for performing needs assessment, intervention planning, programme tracking, and impact evaluation.

* *Module 3 - Introduction to Relational Database using Airtable**

* Define the basic structure and process of constructing a relational database.
* Describe the use of Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) for planning a relational database project.
* Introduce Airtable for implementing a relational database.

* *Module 4 - Program Management with Data Analytics in Airtable**

* Demonstrate the use of Airtable for programme planning and tracking.
* Describe the use of Airtable automation features for streamlining work flow and Airtable interface features for enhancing presentation and reporting.
* Introduce the collaboration features in Airtable for team recruitment and coordination.

* *Module 5 - Design Thinking for Needs Assessment**

* Introduce the Design Thinking process and tools.
* Describe how Design Thinking can be combined with Lean Startup methods to perform need assessment, service intervention, and programme evaluation in the context of a logic model.
* Use of low-fidelity prototype (e.g. wireframes and paper prototype) in user testing.

* *Module 6 - Requirement Specification and Wireframe Prototype**

* Describe the use of story map, entity relationship diagrams, site map, and wireframes for specifying application requirements.
* Describe the flow of data through the application — from story map to wireframes, wireframes to database.
* Develop acceptance criteria for validation and quality control.

* *Module 7 - Web Development in WordPress**

* Introduce the Wordpress content management system and how it can be used for scheduling, donation management, training, volunteers recruitment, case management, e-commerce, service subscription, survey, and services tracking through installation of 3rd party plugins.
* Develop customised data tables for special project data entry, data tracking and reporting.
* Secure Wordpress system operation with user right and access management, scheduled backup, and firewall protection.

* *Module 8 - Workflow Integration through Webhooks and Application Program Interface (API)**

* Introduce the use of REST (**Re**presentational **S**tate **T**ransfer) API for common data exchange between different applications and systems.
* Integrate WordPress and Airtable through web hooks and REST API for shared functions and streamlining operations.
* Describe the importance of API in the formation of digital platforms and business models.

courses.description: This course aims to provide an extensive review of the theoretical foundations of the various schools of marriage and family therapy, from modernism to post-modernism. The focus will be on unifying conceptual threads that integrate different approaches, including Bowenian, strategic, structural, experiential, solution-focused, and narrative. Techniques from various models that are applicable to family therapy with Chinese families will also be addressed. The teaching format includes lecture, videotaped segments of family interviews, role-play, and case discussion.

courses.title: Youth:Risk and Resilience
courses.description: The course examines the differing perspectives of identifying at-risk youth. It aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the at-risk youth in the contexts of peer, family, school and community. With an emphasis on the integration of theory and practice, the course examines different approaches of working with at-risk youth, and analyzes psychological and social intervention strategies that may help in the development of youth resilience. Topical areas of particular relevance to work with youth such as sexuality, non-engaged youth, juvenile delinquency, substance abuse and positive youth development are examined.

courses.description: This course examines the nature and needs of children and youth with special needs including various physical disabilities, intellectual disability, specific learning difficulty, autistic spectrum, and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. The assessment and interventions of these clients and their families will be introduced and the roles of various professionals working with these young people, especially, the role of social worker, will be examined. Relevant education, policy, medical and legal issues are discussed. It also initiates a critical discussion on the evidence-based practice which is built on up-to-date empirical findings in local context, and the challenge of social work intervention in Hong Kong.

courses.description: This course aims to help students understand the development and current situation of social work in contemporary urban China and fully recognize the opportunity and challenges faced by social work in Chinese cities. The course content will include the pilot and model of social work service in different cities, changes in service delivery and funding, development of innovative social management and NGOs. courses.description: This course equips students with different intervention approaches (e.g. client-centered approach, family therapy, group work) in assessing and helping children and youth suffering from mental health problems and/ or mental disorders. * Bio-psycho-social perspectives in childhood and adolescent mental health and its implications for assessment and intervention
* Social stigma and psychosocial effects of psychiatric diagnosis on children and adolescents with mental health needs and their families
* Systemic framework in assessment and management
* Family-centered care in children’s and adolescents’ mental health
* Critical socio-cultural issues (e.g., poverty, traditional Chinese cultural beliefs) in assessment and intervention
* Evidence-based clinical practice

* Family-centered practice and childhood and adolescent disorders such as
+ anxiety disorders
+ depression
+ schizophrenia
+ anorexia nervosa and obesity
+ attention deficit and/or hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
+ learning disorder
+ autistic spectrum disorder
+ intellectual disabilities
* Multiple family groups with families of children and adolescents with mental health needs
* Roles and functions of social workers in family-centered care in children’s and adolescents’ mental health, multidisciplinary teamwork in mental health services, social services and the education sector.

courses.description: This course aims to facilitate students’ professional competence by helping them integrate theory and practice. Students have to critically examine the needs and characteristics of the target groups, the influential social ideologies, related social policies, critical contextual factors and the interconnection of these elements in affecting the well-being of individual and family. In the process of the project, students also have the opportunity to further integrate their knowledge of social work research and practice. According to the results of the study, students have to discuss innovative approaches for improvement or innovative service models in their project reports. In order to facilitate learning, students will be arranged in small groups.
